title: Why 89% of AI Pilots Never Reach Production
author: Jason D.
excerpt: The gap between demo and production isn't technical. It's structural. Here's what the data says and how evaluation-first engineering closes the gap.
content:
The numbers are stark: according to Gartner, 95% of enterprises are running AI pilots. According to Deloitte, only 11% achieve production-grade results. That's an 89% failure rate from pilot to production.

We've worked with enough organizations to see why. The pattern is remarkably consistent.

The Five Failure Modes

1. No Success Criteria

The pilot was launched without defining what "success" means in measurable terms. When it's time to justify production investment, there's no data to support the case.

2. Demo-Driven Development

The team optimized for impressive demos rather than reliable production behavior. The happy path looks great. The edge cases are ignored until they matter.

3. Missing Evaluation Infrastructure

There's no automated way to test the system against known scenarios. Quality is assessed by vibes — someone reviews a few outputs and says "looks good."

4. No Operational Owner

The AI team built it, but nobody in operations owns it. When it breaks at 2 AM, the ticket sits until the AI team gets back from lunch.

5. Misaligned Incentives

The AI team is measured on "innovation." Operations is measured on reliability. These incentives pull in opposite directions.

The Evaluation-First Alternative

Evaluation-first engineering flips the script:

# Traditional approach:
1. Pick a use case
2. Build the model
3. Demo to stakeholders
4. Hope it works in production
5. Wonder why it doesn't

# Evaluation-first approach:
1. Define success criteria (measurable)
2. Build evaluation framework
3. Build the model
4. Test against eval suite
5. Deploy with monitoring
6. Iterate based on data

The difference? Steps 1 and 2 happen before any model work. By the time you build, you already know how to measure success and failure.

What Production-Ready Looks Like

A production-ready AI system has:

  • Automated evaluation running on every change
  • Clear escalation paths for uncertain cases
  • Monitoring dashboards visible to operations
  • An operational owner with clear responsibilities
  • Business KPIs tied directly to agent performance

The gap between demo and production isn't about better models. It's about better engineering practices. Evaluation-first closes that gap.

The Bottom Line

If your AI pilot isn't designed for production from day one, it probably won't get there. Start with evaluation, build for operations, and measure what matters. That's how you beat the 89%.
